episodes.191531: Several strong to severe thunderstorms formed along a dry over eastern Colorado and tracked east through mid afternoon to early evening. Severe hail, up to 3.5 inches, occurred.
episodes.191540: A weak disturbance triggered a couple of thunderstorms that produced localized wind damage over portions of the central Shenandoah Valley.
episodes.191542: A weak disturbance triggered a few thunderstorms that produced low-end gale-force winds over portions of the tidal Potomac River and the middle Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.191598: Scattered thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of July 4, 2024. While these thunderstorms were generally sub-severe, one thunderstorm did produce severe winds in the Springfield area with a spotter estimating winds as much as 60 mph.
episodes.191689: River flooding from late June continued into early July.
episodes.191744: A hot and humid air mass  combined with a weak upper level disturbance helped to spark a line of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of Independence Day that crossed Stokes and Surry counties. This line of storms caused notable wind damage as several trees and power lines were blown down.
episodes.191745: A hot and humid air mass combined with a weak upper level disturbance helped to spark a line of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of Independence Day that crossed Carroll, Henry, and Patrick counties. This line of storms caused notable wind damage as several trees were blown down.
episodes.191971: Slow moving low pressure generated a pocket of prolonged heavy rain over a portion of northeast South Dakota.  Radar estimates of rainfall ranged between 2 and 5 inches in a broad area covering portions of Brown, Day, Clark and Codington counties, with public measurements of between 2.76 and 3.5 inches on the west side of Watertown, and an observed rainfall of 2.85 inches near Ferney. Portions of the Stokes-Thomas Lake City Park campground at Lake Kampeska experienced flooding as a result of this heavy rain. A trained spotter also reported water running over several roads 3 miles north of Bradley in Clark county. This heavy rain was also responsible for minor flooding along Mud Creek and the South Branch Tributary of Mud Creek both near Rauville.
episodes.192045: Isolated thunderstorms produced a landspout tornado near Melvin in Ford County during the afternoon of July 4th.
episodes.192132: A cold front moved into the South Plains on Independence Day serving as a focus for rapid thunderstorm development during the mid to late afternoon hours. Thunderstorms initially developed near the Texas/New Mexico state line from the western South Plains into southeast New Mexico underneath a very hot near surface atmosphere. The hot, deeply mixed lower levels of the atmosphere also supported plenty of potential for evaporative cooling as heavy precipitation fell into the layer from above. The rain-cooled air accelerated downward, creating strong to severe wind gusts as the air hit the ground and spread out. The most intense wind gusts, as high as 80 mph, impacted areas south of Levelland (Hockley County) to north of Ropesville (Hockley County).
episodes.192135: A northeast-southeast oriented cold front from central Kansas across northwest Missouri dropped southeast into the Missouri Ozarks during the afternoon and evening hours on July 3, 2024. Thunderstorms developed along the boundary, bringing hail between 1-3 inches and damaging winds. Of note was 100 mph winds resulting in a cell tower collapsing as well as 3 inch size hail in Stone County. A tornado also occurred in Stone County, resulting in multiple trees to be uprooted or snapped.
episodes.192702: Storms tracked out of northwest Kansas and southwest Nebraska during the early evening hours of Wednesday July 3rd and moved into central Kansas around 11 pm. The line of storms accelerated southeast and produced a large swath of damaging winds as they tracked southeast through the overnight hours.||There were multiple reports of 70 mph winds with the Salina Airport recording an 82 mph wind gust with a mesonet in McPherson county reporting a 76 mph gust. Unfortunately there were 3 injuries and one fatality on Wilson Lake in Russell county when a number of campers were rolled by the strong winds.
episodes.192853: A broad, upper level trough was moving over Nebraska. A surface frontal boundary was across western Nebraska with an upper level disturbance beginning to move overhead. Instability was highest across western portions of the forecast area. Wind shear was fairly high. ||Storms developed across western and northern Nebraska during the early afternoon hours along the frontal boundary. These storms developed into a line and moved southeastward and impacted south central and central Nebraska during the evening hours. The storms began by blowing down tree limbs in Dawson County just after 7 PM CDT. The line of storms ended by producing a 62 mph wind gust in Buffalo County just after 8 PM CDT.
episodes.192987: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193115: Slow moving sea breeze convection over a moist airmass with precipitable water over 2 inches prompted locally heavy rainfall in storms.
episodes.193143: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 4th, along a weak stationary frontal boundary. The strongest storms produced large hail to ping pong ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193169: A line of severe thunderstorms developed along the Nebraska panhandle early in the afternoon on the 3rd with strong outflow winds and up to ping pong ball sized hail. An additional storm developed early in the evening over the northern Nebraska panhandle with strong winds and quarter size hail near Chadron.
episodes.193468: Multiple rounds of scattered storms developed on the evening of July 2 and 3. Both of these events only produced isolated wind damage across central and east-central Kansas, with some flooding also occurring early morning on July 4.
episodes.193643: A broad trough moving across the Great Plains and an advancing front helped to initiate a band of thunderstorms that moved across southeast New Mexico and portions of the Permian Basin. Localized damaging wind gusts and a landspout were reported.
episodes.193644: A broad trough moving across the Great Plains and an advancing front helped to initiate a band of thunderstorms that moved across southeast New Mexico and portions of the Permian Basin. Localized damaging wind gusts and a landspout were reported.
episodes.193685: Thunderstorms developed around midday over portions of the northwestern Sandhills and north central Nebraska. These storms developed ahead of a weak cold front and approaching upper level trough of low pressure. As the afternoon progressed, storms intensified, becoming severe, then persisted into the evening hours across the Sandhills into southwestern Nebraska. Hail up to ping pong ball size, thunderstorm wind gusts to 60 MPH and a tornado were reported with these storms.
episodes.193756: Scattered thunderstorm development occurred across central and southern Oklahoma during the late afternoon into evening of the 4th. This activity was fostered by a cold frontal passage across the aforementioned areas throughout the day. The combination of locally strong instability and modest organizing/deep-layer wind shear favored single and multi-cell thunderstorm modes. The strongest (severe) thunderstorms produced damaging downburst wind gusts and a few reports of hail.
episodes.193930: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles starting late on the 2nd and continuing through the evening of the 3rd. First storms moved from the southeast to northwest, changing over to move west to east motion and finally with the final wave, they moved from the north-northwest to south-southeast. On the evening of the 2nd a couple of isolated storm became severe producing winds up to 70 to 80 mph over Randall and Collingsworth Counties. Then on the evening of the 3rd additional thunderstorms became severe through wind gusts reaching up to 60 to 63 mph in the TX Panhandle and the OK Panhandle.
episodes.193931: Scattered showers and thunderstorms moved across the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles starting late on the 2nd and continuing through the evening of the 3rd. First storms moved from the southeast to northwest, changing over to move west to east motion and finally with the final wave, they moved from the north-northwest to south-southeast. On the evening of the 2nd a couple of isolated storm became severe producing winds up to 70 to 80 mph over Randall and Collingsworth Counties. Then on the evening of the 3rd additional thunderstorms became severe through wind gusts reaching up to 60 to 63 mph in the TX Panhandle and the OK Panhandle.
episodes.194058: Following morning convection over central and southern Iowa tied to a system further south into Missouri, a frontal boundary sweeping across northern into the eastern parts of Iowa by the afternoon to evening resulted in additional showers and thunderstorms. The parameter space overhead included MLCAPE values of 1000+ J/kg and deep layer shear around 40-50+ knots. In particular, Cerro Gordo county received severe thunderstorm wind damage, with estimated gusts around 58 mph. Otherwise, no other reports were received for this particular event.
episodes.194071: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Nebraska which led to a 63 mph wind gust at the McCook Airport.
episodes.194072: Thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado during the afternoon and produced multiple recorded wind gusts around 60 mph and some tree damage in Yuma county. Hail up to quarter size was also reported north of the town of Yuma.
episodes.194073: Thunderstorms that originated from eastern Colorado moved into western Kansas producing numerous instances of severe wind up to 70 mph. Tree damage from thunderstorm winds was reported in Rawlins county along with nickel size hail.
episodes.194176: During the evening on July 4th, a line of thunderstorms moved across portions of the Upper Mississippi River Valley producing localized wind damage in Chickasaw County. These storms also disrupted numerous Independence Day festivities across the area.
episodes.194216: A strong upper level wave and associated cold front sparked an isolated strong storm along the Minnesota-Iowa border during the very early afternoon which produced spotty large hail and a funnel cloud.
episodes.194290: Thunderstorms developed as a broad upper low circulated over North Dakota. One thunderstorm produced a landspout tornado to the southeast of Chaseley, in Wells County. The tornado occurred in an open field and damaged no structures, thus by National Weather Service policy the tornado was rated EF-U (Unknown).
episodes.194360: Elevated water levels flowing down the Mississippi River from locations north of the Quad State resulted in minor flooding on the Mississippi in Southeast Missouri from early to mid July. Impacts were mostly limited to low-lying agricultural areas.
episodes.194375: Storms moved through Southwest Indiana during the late afternoon and early evening hours as a cold front crossed the region. One storm downed a power line in Francisco. Effective bulk shear was 30 kts while MLCAPE was 2000 J/kg ahead of the front. PW values were very high, up to 2.4 inches, producing robust rainfall rates. Flash flooding occurred in multiple locations in Southwest Indiana.
episodes.194378: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the heat of the day on Independence Day, with wind gusts estimated to 60 mph near Hopkinsville. MLCAPE values exceeded 3000 J/kg. While effective bulk shear was 30-40 kts, 0-3km SRH was near 100 m2/s2. Lapse rates were fairly limited at around 5 C/km.
episodes.194452: A morning line of thunderstorms progressed through Southwest Indiana during the morning hours on Independence Day. Strong downdraft winds damaged or blew down around a dozen trees in the Woodland Lake area southwest of Evansville. MLCAPE was around 1500 J/kg while effective bulk shear was near 40 kts.
episodes.194491: From around 5:30 pm through the late evening, thunderstorms moved across an area of the westernmost counties in sw Kansas, with primarily strong but sub severe criteria wind gusts of up to 55 mph. One severe criterion wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at the HAYS airport around 11 pm.  Isolated hail was also occurring, evidenced by the public report of penny sized hail near Friend, KS.
episodes.194641: A line of showers and storms developed ahead of an approaching cold front, moving across northeastern Kentucky in the afternoon. Additional storms formed ahead of the line, in far eastern Kentucky. Within the line of storms, one cell in particular became strong and resulted in severe thunderstorm warnings across multiple counties. This storm did result in straight line wind damage in portions of Rowan and Elliott Counties.
episodes.194649: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced gusty winds across portions of the York River.
episodes.194722: Afternoon and evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay area and Fort Myers area near the mouth of the Caloosahatchee River.
episodes.194867: Westerly flow initiated thunderstorms over region bringing severe wind and hail to the eastern plains.
episodes.194931: Rain that fell during the month of June across Minnesota and Wisconsin caused rises on the Mississippi River along the Iowa and Illinois border. Additionally, heavy rain that fell locally in July helped to prolong the crest and delay the river falling below flood stage, especially south of the Wapsipinicon, Rock, and Iowa Rivers.
episodes.194946: Rain that fell during the month of June across Minnesota and Wisconsin caused rises on the Mississippi River, along the Iowa and Illinois border. Additionally, heavy rain that fell locally in July helped to prolong the crest and delay the river falling below flood stage, especially south of the Wapsipinicon, Rock, and Iowa Rivers.
episodes.195056: In an environment characterized by boundary collisions and high instability, a storm over Lake Pontchartrain was able to take advantage of the vorticity of the boundaries and produce a waterspout.
episodes.195212: A slow-moving cold front lingered across the Ohio Valley, bringing multiple waves of showers and thunderstorms from July 3rd through July 5th. Localized training of heavier showers and thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding, particularly in Dubois County during the afternoon and evening hours on July 3rd. Over this three day period, scattered strong to severe storms produced mainly isolated straight-line wind damage across southern Indiana, though one spin-up EF0 tornado touched down in Harrison County on July 4th. The cold front finally pushed through the region during the evening hours on July 5th, bringing an end to the active weather.
episodes.195213: A slow-moving cold front lingered near the Ohio Valley from July 3rd through July 5th, with multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms moving through the area during this time period. While most of the thunderstorms were not severe, a few instances of wind damage were observed in the Louisville metro. Additionally, a brief spin-up EF1 tornado occurred in west Louisville on July 4th. The cold front finally moved through the area during the evening on July 5th, bringing an end to this period of active weather.
episodes.195542: Three funnel clouds were reported; all of them were associated with small showers.

The tornado initially caused a broad swath of damage, with the damage path becoming more narrow before lifting.  ||The damage began to a Baptist Fellowship Center just north of |Woodland Avenue along Catalpa Street. The nearby church sustained shingle |damage, but also had some window damage on the more protected |north facing side of the building. South of Woodland Avenue, a |witness saw twisting motion, and there a black walnut tree branch |fell to the west onto a neighbor's house and a tree from that home |fell onto his truck.  As the tornado tightened up, several tree|branches fell onto vehicles and structures.  A few bigger trees|were uprooted as well, including one that pulled down some power|poles as it fell.  In another place, the tornado pulled back part|of a roof on a two-story residence.  Farther east, the vinyl|siding was stripped off a north-facing wall of another two-story|residence.  ||As the tornado continued east and east southeast, crossing Wilson Avenue, it narrowed quite a bit, causing more isolated tree damage before it lifted just east of 23rd Street and north of Standard Avenue.
